extraction_text: Yakshas, Rakshasas, and Gandharvas attack Bhima with various weapons.
Bhima fights back with his arrows, destroying their weapons and piercing their limbs.

A Rakshasa named Maniman, a friend of Kubera, appears, displaying great strength and valor.
The rakshasa (demon) mocked the fleeing rakshasas for being defeated by a mortal and questioned how they would explain this to their lord Kubera.
The rakshasa (Hidimba) prevented the other rakshasas from fleeing and charged at Bhima with weapons.
Bhima shot three arrows that struck Hidimba's sides.
Enraged, Hidimba threw a club at Bhima, who countered by throwing his own club.
Hidimba threw a golden-shafted iron spear that grazed Bhima's right arm and fell to the ground.
Bhima, wounded but skilled in club warfare, grabbed his steel club and charged at Hidimba with a roar.
Hidimba threw a shining iron trident, which Bhima shattered with his club.
Bhima leapt into the air and threw his club, which struck Hidimba and killed him.

supernatural_elements: Comparison to Indra wielding the vajra

extraction_text: The remaining rakshasas, seeing Hidimba dead, fled eastward with terrible cries.

The Pandava brothers embraced Bhima and sat together on the mountaintop.
